parts.label: Part 2
parts.article:
Ladies and Gentlemen, welcome to Auckland Zoo on this sunny Sunday afternoon, and to our special Kiwi fundraising event. My job is to tell you all about the amazing little kiwi, and your job, hopefully, is to dig deep into your pockets!

Now, for the benefit of our overseas visitors here today, I should explain first of all that the kiwi is the national bird of New Zealand — and sometimes New Zealanders themselves are known as Kiwis.

Now, while kiwis in the wild are a rare sight, the kiwi as a symbol is far more visible. Apart from being in toy stores and airport shops all over the world, you'll find them on our stamps and coins. The kiwi is the smallest member of the genus Apteryx, which also includes ostriches and emus. It gets its name from its shrill call, which sounds very much like this: "kee-wee, kee-wee." Kiwis live in forests or swamps and feed on insects, worms, snails, and berries. It’s a nocturnal bird with limited sight, and therefore it has to rely on its very keen sense of smell to find food and to sense danger. Its nostrils are actually located right at the end of its long beak, which is one-third of its body length.

Now here’s an interesting fact: Although kiwis have wings, they serve little purpose because the kiwi is a flightless bird. Since the settlement of New Zealand by Europeans, kiwi numbers have dropped from 12 million to less than 70,000, and our national bird is rapidly becoming an endangered species. This is because they’re being threatened by what we call "introduced animals" — animals that were brought to New Zealand, such as cats and ferrets, which eat kiwi eggs and chicks.

And so, we’ve launched the Kiwi Recovery Programme in an all-out effort to save our national bird from extinction. There are three stages to this Programme: Firstly, we have the scientific research stage — this involves research to learn more about what kiwis need to survive in the wild. Then, secondly, we have the action stage. This is where we go into the field and actually put our knowledge to work — we call this putting science into practice. Finally, we come to the third stage: the global education stage. By working with schools and groups like yours, as well as through our award-winning kiwi website, we hope to educate people about the plight of the kiwi.

As part of the action stage, which I just mentioned, we’ve introduced "Operation Nest Egg," and this is where your money will be going. It works like this: It’s a three-stage process. First, we go out to the kiwi’s natural habitat and collect kiwi eggs. This is the tricky part, because it can be very difficult to find the eggs. Then, in safe surroundings, away from predators... the chicks are reared. Now, this can be done on predator-free islands or in captivity — they are reared until they are about nine months old, at which stage the chicks are returned to the wild. So far, it’s proving successful, and since we started the programme, some 34 chicks have been successfully raised this year. Their chances of survival have increased from 5% to 85%. However, it’s not time to celebrate kiwi survival just yet. About 95% of kiwi chicks still don’t make it to six months of age without protection. That’s why Operation Nest Egg is so important, and we ask you to give generously today.

analyses.content: 介绍中提到，除了在玩具店和机场商店，你还能在纽西兰的 stamps and coins（邮票和硬币）上找到几维鸟的图片。
Apart from being in toy stores and airport shops all over the world, you'll find them on our stamps and coins.
听到 "Apart from"（除了...之外）要意识到后面提到的 "toy stores" 是用来排除或者是次要信息，重点在主句提到的物品。
It gets its name from its shrill call, which sounds very much like this: "kee-wee, kee-wee."
不要填 "name" 或 "sound"，原文具体的描述是 "shrill call"，且紧接着模仿了 "kee-wee" 的声音。
录音明确说这种鸟的名字来源于它那尖锐的 call（叫声/鸣叫）。
It’s a nocturnal bird with limited sight, and therefore it has to rely on its very keen sense of smell to find food and to sense danger.
题目中有 "poor sight but a good..."，这是典型的转折对比，录音中用 "limited sight" 和 "keen sense of smell" 对应。
几维鸟视力（sight）很差，所以不得不依赖其非常敏锐的 sense of smell（嗅觉）来寻找食物。
Although kiwis have wings, they serve little purpose because the kiwi is a flightless bird.
千万不要填 adjectives（形容词） "flightless"，语法上 "cannot flightless" 是不通的。
虽然有翅膀，但几维鸟是 "flightless bird"（不会飞的鸟），题目中 "cannot ..." 需要填动词原形 fly。
This is because they’re being threatened by what we call "introduced animals" — animals that were brought to New Zealand, such as cats and ferrets...
不要只填 "cats and ferrets"，那只是举例（such as...），题目需要填这一类动物的总称。
几维鸟受到所谓的 introduced animals（引进动物）的威胁，如猫和雪貂。

analyses.content: 录音中提到该计划有三个阶段，第一个阶段就是 scientific research（科学研究）阶段，涉及研究生存需求。
Firstly, we have the scientific research stage — this involves research to learn more about what kiwis need to survive in the wild.
听到 "Firstly" 后紧跟的名词短语就是答案，不要漏掉 "scientific"。
Finally, we come to the third stage: the global education stage. By working with schools and groups like yours...
表格题要注意横向对应，看到 "schools and the website" 就要去听这一阶段的特定名称。
这一阶段涉及与学校和网站合作，录音称之为 global education（全球教育）阶段。

analyses.content: First, we go out to the kiwi’s natural habitat and collect kiwi eggs.
题目主语是 People，谓语动词需要原形，不要只填 eggs，动作 "collect" 也是关键信息。
流程图的第一步，人们去自然栖息地 collect kiwi eggs（收集几维鸟蛋）。
Then, in safe surroundings, away from predators... the chicks are reared.
这是一个被动语态的填空，虽然前面隔了很长的插入语（in safe surroundings...），但核心动作是雏鸟被抚养。
在安全的各种环境中，远离捕食者，chicks are reared（雏鸟被抚养/饲养）。
Their chances of survival have increased from 5% to 85%. However, it’s not time to celebrate kiwi survival just yet. About 95% of kiwi chicks still don’t make it...
听到 "95%" 别急着填，那是没有保护就活不下来的比例；也要避开 "34" 这个具体的雏鸟数量。题目卷面上如果有 % 号，横线上只写数字 85 即可。
几维鸟的存活率从 5% 增加到了 85%。
